blocks.content: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is the only confirmed active volcano in India and the South Asia region.

rows: Layered cone of ash and lava

items: Note the difference between India's Barren Island (Active) and Narcondam Island (Dormant/Extinct).
Deccan Traps in Peninsular India are classic examples of Flood Basalt Provinces created by ancient volcanic activity.
Calderas represent the most explosive volcanic landforms, which collapse inward during eruptions forming large depressions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Magma refers to molten rock stored beneath Earth's crust, while lava is molten rock that breaks through to the surface.
The Circum-Pacific Belt, known as the 'Ring of Fire', contains over 75% of the world's active volcanoes.
Barren Island in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is the only active volcano located in India and South Asia.
Shield volcanoes are primarily composed of basaltic lava, making them less steep and largely non-explosive.
Composite volcanoes (Stratovolcanoes) erupt cooler, more viscous lava accompanied by large quantities of pyroclastic material and ash.
